list.heading: Servers
list.unset: Set where {count, plural, one {{name} lives} other {# servers live}}: a home server behind a router and a data-center box are exposed in different ways, so Polaris needs the answer before it can tell you how to point a domain.
list.rowHint: Right-click for more, F2 to rename
list.empty: Add a server to reach it from Containers (Docker), Drive (SFTP) and a shell here.
list.reachBody: Run this on the machine Polaris runs on to give it a shell, its files, and a login to run jobs under.

shell.asRoot: Signed in as {login} over SSH, elevated with sudo.

environment.title: Where does {name} live?
environment.intro: This decides how a domain can be pointed at it, and whether it can serve public traffic directly. Registered servers can also take a wildcard domain of their own below.
environment.detected: Polaris detected {name} from its address. Confirm it or pick another.
environment.wildcardHint: Point *.{domain} at this server, and its services get a real domain with a Let's Encrypt certificate. Leave empty to use free IP-based subdomains.

host.intro: An SSH host, reusable in Containers (Docker) and Drive (SFTP).
host.name: Name

enroll.notRegistered: The machine could not be registered
enroll.expiredAfter: {reason} This command has since expired, so generate a new one.
enroll.expired: This command expired before the machine ran it
enroll.runOnce: Run this on the server. It works once and expires {minutes, plural, =0 {in under a minute} other {in # min}}.
enroll.lanLabel: Point the command at the local address
enroll.lan: This server cannot reach the internet. Point the command at {base} instead, which only works from the same network.
enroll.insecureLan: The local address has no certificate, so this command pipes an unencrypted download into a root shell. It stays on your own network, which is the trade being made.
enroll.insecure: Polaris is only reachable over plain HTTP here, so this command pipes an unencrypted download into a root shell. Set a domain with HTTPS under Admin > Domains before running it on anything you do not fully trust the network of.
enroll.stillUsable: It was not used, so the command above still works. Fix that and run it again before it expires - this picks it up on its own.
enroll.waiting: Waiting for the server to check in...
enroll.introLocal: Polaris runs in a container, so it reaches this machine through its container engine and nothing else - which is why it has no shell here. Run this command on the machine itself and it joins like any other server: a dedicated polaris login with no password, authorized for one key Polaris keeps.
enroll.intro: Polaris generates a command you run on the server. It creates a dedicated polaris login with no password, authorizes one key Polaris keeps, and registers the machine. No credential of yours is typed anywhere.
enroll.name: Name (optional)
enroll.namePlaceholder: Its hostname is used when you leave this empty
enroll.grants: The command adds a dedicated login, lets it manage containers and gives it password-less sudo, which is what deploying, CI jobs and the file browser need. Undo it later by deleting the login and /etc/sudoers.d/polaris.

refusals.ssh-not-listening: The machine stopped before registering: nothing Polaris could reach is listening on its SSH port. Start its SSH server, or bind it to something other than loopback.
refusals.remote-login-off: The machine stopped before registering: Remote Login is off, so nothing would answer Polaris. Turn it on under System Settings > General > Sharing, where you can also see which logins it lets in.
refusals.ssh-access-list-unrestricted: The machine stopped before registering: Remote Login is off there, and its SSH access list either lets every account on that machine in or would not say - turning Remote Login on would then have opened every account there, which is wider than this command grants, so it was left off exactly as found. Look at which logins that list admits under System Settings > General > Sharing > Remote Login; turning Remote Login on is yours to decide once you have.
refusals.remote-login-unrestricted: The machine stopped before registering: Remote Login could not be limited to the ''{login}'' login, and turning it on for every account there is wider than this command grants, so it was left off the way the command found it. Turn it on and restrict it to that login under System Settings > General > Sharing.
refusals.remote-login-left-open: The machine stopped before registering: Remote Login was turned on there, could not be limited to the ''{login}'' login, and could not be confirmed back off - every account on that machine may be reachable over SSH right now. Turn Remote Login off, or restrict it to that login, under System Settings > General > Sharing.
refusals.ssh-access-list-left-behind: The machine stopped before registering: SSH there was limited to the ''{login}'' login before Remote Login was turned on, and the machine then would not say whether Remote Login is on or off - so that limit was left in place rather than taken off a machine that may be reachable. Until it is removed, SSH there admits that login and nothing else: run 'sudo dseditgroup -o delete com.apple.access_ssh' on the machine to put SSH back to every account, and check Remote Login under System Settings > General > Sharing.
refusals.not-in-ssh-access-list: The machine stopped before registering: it limits SSH to a list of logins, ''{login}'' is not on it, and the command could not add it - so the machine would have turned Polaris away. Add that login under System Settings > General > Sharing > Remote Login. Remote Login itself was left exactly as the command found it.
refusals.no-ssh-host-keys: The machine stopped before registering: it has no SSH host keys and none could be generated. Install an SSH server there.
refusals.no-home-directory: The machine stopped before registering: the ''{login}'' login has no home directory, so the key could not be installed. Fix the account.
refusals.no-user-tooling: The machine stopped before registering: it has neither useradd nor adduser, so the login could not be created. Create a ''{login}'' user there.
refusals.unsupported-platform: The machine stopped before registering: its operating system is not one the command supports. Add this server by hand instead.
refusals.curl-missing: The machine stopped before registering: curl is not installed there. Install it.
refusals.unknown-option: The machine stopped before registering: the command was run with an argument it does not know. Paste it exactly as Polaris printed it.
refusals.not-root: The machine stopped before registering: the command was not run as root. Run it with sudo.

disconnect.label: Disconnect it
disconnect.summary: Polaris forgets the server and stops managing it. Whatever is running there keeps running, and its login stays authorized.

clean.label: Disconnect it and clean up
clean.summary: Stop the services Polaris deployed there and take its login back off the machine first, so nothing is left running unmanaged.

move.label: Move its services first, then clean up
move.summary: Each service comes up on the new server before the old one is stopped, so it is not off while it moves. Then the machine is cleaned up and forgotten.

remove.partlyMoved: {reason}. Moved first: {names}. The server is still connected.
remove.intro: Polaris stops reaching this machine. What happens to what it is running is up to you.
remove.volumes: {count, plural, one {One volume on this machine is} other {# volumes on this machine are}} re-created empty on the new server. Copy anything you need off it first.
remove.moving: Moving the services. Each one is a full deploy, so this takes a few minutes - leave this open.
remove.nothing: Nothing is deployed on this server.
remove.services: {count, plural, one {# service} other {# services}} live here{running, plural, =0 {} other {, # running right now}}.
remove.pools: {count, plural, one {# runner pool} other {# runner pools}} lose the machine they run on.

storage.switchFailed: Could not change it. Try again.
storage.deleteBody: {size} of whatever was written in it, gone for good. Nothing on this machine references it{dated, select, yes {, and it was created {created}} other {}}. A volume does not come back the way a rebuilt image does.
storage.volumesIntro: Largest first. A volume is where an app keeps what it wrote - a database, a world, an upload.
storage.autoRemoveUnread: Could not read whether this is on.
storage.autoRemoveHint: The data of an app deleted over a week ago that nothing has used since. You are told what went.
storage.reading: Reading what this machine is holding
storage.noVolumesBody: Nothing on this machine has stored anything in a volume yet.
storage.noRecord: Polaris has no record of this one
storage.spare: {count, plural, one {One volume is} other {# volumes are}} holding {size} that nothing on this machine references, that Polaris has no record of, and that has been sitting there for more than a day. Delete them one at a time, when you know what they were.
storage.filesIntro: What the containers on this machine are holding is above. The files people put here are Drive's side of the same disk, and it weighs its own folders.
storage.driveRoom: What is taking up room in Drive
storage.heldBy: held by {names}{rest, plural, =0 {} other { and # more}}
storage.removeBody: Polaris deployed this and no longer has a record of it{running, select, yes {, and it is still running} other {}}. Removing it frees its image layer and its ports. Anything it wrote to a volume stays where it is - those are listed above, with their sizes.
storage.leftBehindIntro: Polaris put {count, plural, one {this container} other {these # containers}} on this machine and has no record of {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} any more - a service removed, or a stack recreated under another name. Nothing else on the machine is touched.

reach.local: Running Polaris, so it is up by definition.

connect.localNote: Polaris has no login of its own on this machine, so there is nothing to copy here. Sign in the way you already do, or add it with Add server to get a shell and its files in Polaris too.
connect.keyNote: The key Polaris uses stays in Polaris, so these connect with your own credentials for that account.
connect.passwordNote: Use the password this server was registered with.

lan.title: On this network
lan.intro: Polaris reaches this server at {address}. A direct address on this network is faster and keeps working when the internet does not - and if the machine has moved, this is what finds it again.
lan.foundMoved: It is not where Polaris had it recorded any more. <mono>{address}</mono> is this same server - its host key proves it.
lan.none: It has no address on this network, so it really is somewhere else.
lan.unreachable: It is not answering where Polaris knows it, and nothing on this network answers with its host key. It is switched off, or somewhere else.
lan.unknown: Polaris does not know its own address on this network, so it cannot tell what is near it.

detail.loadHint: Read from the machine itself, not only from what Polaris runs on it.
detail.seeDisk: See what is taking up the disk
detail.locationHint: A home server behind a router and a data-center box are exposed in different ways, so this decides how a domain is pointed at it.
detail.giveUpHint: The machine Polaris runs on stays listed. Only the SSH login it was enrolled with is given back, so the shell and its files stop being offered here.
detail.removeHint: What this would take with it is worked out first, and anything deployed here can be moved to another server rather than lost.

space.title: Container storage
space.deleteCacheBody: It is only what past builds left to speed up the next ones. Nothing running is affected; the next build of each app takes longer while it is made again.
space.reclaimable: About {size} of that is build cache and images nothing is running. Freeing it costs nothing but the time to build or pull them again - an app that is stopped keeps its data and fetches its image on the next start. Your volumes are not touched, and a release kept for a rollback is not either.
space.nothingWorth: There is nothing worth reclaiming here. Volumes are never touched by this.

groups.title: Server groups
groups.intro: Write a firewall rule once for a set of machines. Adding a server to a group brings it under the group's rules straight away.
groups.enrollFirst: Enroll a server to put one in here.
groups.deleteBody: The servers themselves stay. Any firewall rules written for this group are deleted with it.

usage.offMaybe: It may be off or unreachable.
usage.unread: Polaris could not read this server just now. {reason}
usage.nothing: Nothing worth reporting is running on this server.

edge.title: Serving its own domains
edge.elsewhere: Polaris is setting this server up now. This can take a few minutes.
edge.asking: Asking this server what it is running...
edge.traefikYes: It answers on 80 and 443 itself, so a domain pointed here keeps working while Polaris is off.
edge.traefikNo: Nothing here is answering on 80 and 443, so a domain pointed at this server reaches nothing.
edge.guardYes: The firewall's decision-maker is running beside it.
edge.guardNo: No firewall decision-maker: an address allowlist still applies, a denylist, a rule pack or a sign-in rule cannot.
edge.pushYes: It takes routes and firewall changes from Polaris as they happen.
edge.pushNo: It only reads what a deployed container tells it, so a new domain or an edited firewall rule waits for that service to be built again, and a deploy replaces the running version with a short gap.
edge.offlineYes: Bans and signed-out sessions are kept on this server, so they still apply while Polaris is off.
edge.offlineNo: Bans and signed-out sessions from Polaris do not reach this server yet. Set it up again to fix that.
edge.hint: Installs Docker if it is missing, and starts this server's own edge. It replaces the running one, so anything this server is serving stops for a second or two.
